intro.title: Test useFetch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that fetches and displays a list of users from a public API. You will learn how to write a unit test for a custom React hook, `useFetch`, which handles data fetching. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the React Testing Library. By the end, you'll understand how to test asynchronous logic and manage loading and error states in your tests.
intro.usecase: Testing custom hooks like useFetch is essential for building reliable data-driven applications such as e-commerce product listings, financial dashboards, or social media feeds. In real-world scenarios, developers need to ensure that data fetching logic correctly handles loading states, error responses, and successful data retrieval before integrating it into production UIs. For example, when building an admin panel that displays user analytics, thorough testing of the useFetch hook prevents UI glitches and ensures smooth user experiences. This practice is crucial for maintaining application stability when fetching data from APIs in customer-facing features like search filters, live notifications, or dynamic content modules.
